reason: Section 139 separates assessment-roll content and calculations from certification, validity, and delivery to the treasurer.

proposedGroups.reason: These subsections list roll columns, clerk calculations, form variation, and warrant attachment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the required local improvement assessment roll columns and how the clerk enters frontage, rate, assessment, instalment, and warrant information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Roll certification validity and delivery to treasurer
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address certification after appeals, validity, binding effect, and delivery to the treasurer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the local improvement assessment roll becomes valid and binding and what roll information the clerk delivers to the treasurer.

reason: The section states a single clerk duty to endorse a precept on the assessment roll.

evidenceText: The clerk shall endorse on such assessment roll a precept

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a focused precept endorsement requirement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that the clerk must endorse a prescribed precept on the assessment roll.

reason: The section is a focused lien rule for special frontage assessment instalments.

evidenceText: each instalment payable thereon, from the date it becomes due and payable, shall be a lien

proposedGroups.reason: The target states that each due instalment is a lien.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a special frontage assessment instalment becomes a lien on the abutting parcel.

reason: The section lists by-law powers for collection and recovery of assessments.

evidenceText: prescribe the terms and conditions for

proposedGroups.reason: The target authorizes by-laws about collection, recovery, discounts, penalties, default proceedings, and commutations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the terms and conditions council may prescribe for assessment collection, discounts, penalties, default proceedings, and cash commutations.

reason: The section is a focused rule about when special frontage assessment is not treated as an encumbrance on land.

evidenceText: shall not as between a vendor and a purchaser

proposedGroups.reason: The target states that non-arrears assessments are not deemed encumbrances for listed purposes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a special frontage assessment is not deemed an encumbrance between vendor and purchaser or under specified covenants.

reason: The section states an alternative to cost-based special frontage assessment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Uniform unit rate for local improvement work

evidenceText: the council may by by-law fix a uniform unit rate for a class of work

proposedGroups.reason: The target authorizes a uniform unit rate by by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that council may fix a uniform unit rate for a class of local improvement work instead of basing assessment on work cost.

reason: The section is a focused no-invalidity rule for omitted special frontage assessment notices.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of failing to deliver assessment notice

evidenceText: The omission to deliver any notice in no way affects the liability

proposedGroups.reason: The target states that omitted notice does not affect liability or enforcement validity.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that omission to deliver notice does not affect liability for special frontage assessment or enforcement validity.

reason: The section addresses apportioning a special frontage assessment after subdivision of an abutting parcel.

evidenceText: When an abutting parcel against which a special frontage assessment is in effect, is divided

proposedGroups.reason: The target states how the clerk may apportion the balance with owners’ written consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a special frontage assessment balance and lien may be apportioned when an assessed abutting parcel is divided.

reason: The section is a focused agreement power for local improvement work at an owner’s expense.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Agreement with owner for local improvement work

evidenceText: The municipality may enter into an agreement with the owner of any land

proposedGroups.reason: The target authorizes an owner agreement for local improvement work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipality may enter an agreement with a landowner to provide local improvement work at the owner’s expense in whole or in part.

reason: Section 148 separates local-improvement agreement conditions for subdivision approval from conditions for building permits.

evidenceText: to impose as a condition to the approval of a subdivision of land within the municipality

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph (a) authorizes by-laws imposing owner agreements as subdivision approval conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council may require an owner local-improvement agreement as a condition of subdivision approval.

evidenceText: to impose as a condition to the issue of a building permit for the erection of any building or structure

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraph (b) authorizes by-laws imposing owner agreements as building permit conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council may require an owner local-improvement agreement as a condition of issuing a building permit.

reason: This target only applies the local-improvement provisions in sections 117 to 148 to rural communities.
The section defines a single term for this part.

proposedGroups.reason: The target defines association for this part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that association means a corporation incorporated under this part.

reason: The section governs issuing letters patent to local improvement associations and applying the Companies Act.

proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address incorporation by letters patent, purposes, and Companies Act application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may receive letters patent for a local improvement association, the association’s purposes, and how the Companies Act applies.

reason: The section states a single naming requirement for an association.

evidenceText: An association shall be named the Local Improvement Association

proposedGroups.reason: The target states the required association name format.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an association is named the Local Improvement Association of the municipality for which it is incorporated.

reason: The section is a focused incorporation fee and advertising rule for an association.

evidenceText: No fee is payable on the incorporation of an association

proposedGroups.reason: The target states no incorporation fee is payable and advertising is unnecessary.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that incorporating an association requires no fee and no advertising.

reason: The section states a single prohibition on association share certificates and dividends.

evidenceText: An association shall not issue share certificates or pay dividends.

proposedGroups.reason: The target is a focused prohibition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an association must not issue share certificates or pay dividends.

reason: The section states a single property-holding power and value limit for an association.

evidenceText: An association may hold real and personal property

proposedGroups.reason: The target allows property holding within the letters patent value limit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an association may hold real and personal property up to the value fixed by its letters patent.

reason: The section states a single gift-acceptance power for an association subject to section 154 and any trust or condition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Association gifts donations bequests and devises

evidenceText: An association may receive, hold and use gifts, donations, bequests or devises

proposedGroups.reason: The target authorizes gifts, donations, bequests, and devises subject to stated limits and conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that an association may receive, hold, and use gifts, donations, bequests, or devises subject to property limits and any trust or condition.
